sections.html: Zungaro zungaro is one of the largest catfish species of South America. It reaches a length of up to 140 cm and a weight of up to 50 kg.

Such giants are only suitable for zoos, show aquariums and specialists with correspondingly large tanks. Juveniles of 15-20 cm length, still carrying the juvenile markings, have been imported from Brazil.
Z. zungaro occurs in the Amazon and Orinoco rivers. The very similar Z. jahu, which grows to exactly the same size, comes from the Paraná-Paraguay system.

There were all kinds of debates about its name; for a long time it sailed under Pseudopimelodus zungaro or Paulicea luetkeni. Because of its gigantic size the species is difficult to study, and it undergoes an enormous colour change from a leopard-like patterned juvenile to a monochrome grey giant.

DNA studies suggest that there are other species besides the two generally recognized Zungaro species.
